title: Service Request #5: Dude, Where's My Car?

sentences.en: Well, I thought my car had been stolen, which I was like, does that even happen?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我以为我的车被偷了，当时我就想，这种事真的会发生吗？

sentences.en: I guess it does.
sentences.zh: 我想确实会。

sentences.en: But, you know, my car is really old.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我的车真的很旧了。

sentences.en: It's like 2011 Mazda 6.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆2011年的马自达6。

sentences.en: So I really didn't know why anyone would want to take that car.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的不知道为什么会有人想偷那辆车。

sentences.en: This is Kelly Prime.
sentences.zh: 这位是凯莉·普莱姆（Kelly Prime）。

sentences.en: We work together at 99PI and she lives in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 我们在99PI一起工作，她住在布鲁克林。

sentences.en: And not too long ago, she had an experience that shook her.
sentences.zh: 不久前，她经历了一件让她心有余悸的事。

sentences.en: She and her friends had been out for the day in Coney Island.
sentences.zh: 那天她和朋友们在康尼岛玩了一整天。

sentences.en: And they were stopping to get some takeout on the way home.
sentences.zh: 回家的路上，他们停下来买点外卖。

sentences.en: They were looking for a place to park, not too far from the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他们正在找一个离餐馆不太远的停车位。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is Brooklyn, so there's not a lot of parking available.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是在布鲁克林，所以停车位并不多。

sentences.en: And all the street parking looked like it was filled up.
sentences.zh: 所有的路边停车位看起来都停满了。

sentences.en: But on the right-hand side, we come upon this brightly lit, beautiful, empty parking lot in front of a 7-Eleven.
sentences.zh: 但在右手边，我们发现了一家7-Eleven门前有一个灯火通明、漂亮且空荡荡的停车场。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 太完美了。

sentences.en: Like irresistible, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来简直让人无法抗拒。

sentences.en: Irresistible.
sentences.zh: 无法抗拒。

sentences.en: An oasis.
sentences.zh: 简直是绿洲。

sentences.en: A lure, some might say.
sentences.zh: 有人可能会说，那是个诱饵。

sentences.en: So we parked in the parking lot, pulled up, only car there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就把车停进了停车场，开过去，那是里面唯一的一辆车。

sentences.en: What a miracle.
sentences.zh: 真是奇迹。

sentences.en: And just ran out into the supermarket and spent probably, like, you know, 15 minutes grabbing our stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后我们跑进超市，大概花了15分钟买东西。

sentences.en: They came back out, went to the 7-Eleven parking lot, and the car wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 他们出来回到7-Eleven停车场时，车不见了。

sentences.en: Disappeared.
sentences.zh: 消失了。

sentences.en: The car was gone.
sentences.zh: 车没了。

sentences.en: And I was sort of in denial for a second.
sentences.zh: 那一瞬间我有点不敢相信。

sentences.en: I was like, well, surely.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，肯定还在。

sentences.en: Like, I just, I'm not that great at remembering where I parked anyway.
sentences.zh: 我只是，反正我不太擅长记住自己把车停在哪儿了。

sentences.en: But it's not a big lot, and it's super brightly lit, and there's no cars there.
sentences.zh: 但那停车场不大，灯光又特别亮，而且里面一辆车都没有。

sentences.en: So she and her friends went into the 7-Eleven to ask if anyone had seen anything.
sentences.zh: 于是她和朋友们走进7-Eleven，问有没有人看到什么。

sentences.en: We go to the register, and we're like, I think our car just got stolen.
sentences.zh: 我们走到收银台前说，我想我们的车刚被偷了。

sentences.en: Did you see anyone steal a car?
sentences.zh: 你们有没有看到有人偷车？

sentences.en: And the guy was like, no, it didn't get stolen, got towed.
sentences.zh: 那个人说，不，没被偷，是被拖走了。

sentences.en: And this guy is just acting like, like he's never heard something more boring in his life.
sentences.zh: 那个人表现得好像他这辈子从没听过比这更无聊的事一样。

sentences.en: And he was like, yeah, like, 20 cars get towed a day.
sentences.zh: 他说，是啊，每天大概有20辆车被拖走。

sentences.en: There's a sign out there, call the number.
sentences.zh: 外面有牌子，打上面的电话吧。

sentences.en: Back out in the parking lot, they did find signs warning that unauthorized cars would be towed.
sentences.zh: 回到停车场，他们确实找到了警告违规车辆会被拖走的标志。

sentences.en: One was in Cyrillic, one was covered in graffiti, and another was tucked away in a far corner of the lot.
sentences.zh: 一个是用西里尔字母写的，一个被涂鸦覆盖，另一个则被藏在停车场的一个远角里。

sentences.en: Kelly had the idea to pull up the Google reviews for the 7-Eleven.
sentences.zh: 凯莉想到了去查这家7-Eleven的谷歌评论。

sentences.en: And they found dozens of people telling pretty much the same story.
sentences.zh: 他们发现几十个人讲的几乎是同一个故事。

sentences.en: It says, I was their customer for many years, gave a great business for all those years,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，我多年来一直是他们的顾客，多年来为他们贡献了很好的生意，

sentences.en: till my car was towed, less than six minutes absence.
sentences.zh: 直到我的车被拖走，离开不到六分钟。

sentences.en: If you read the other one-star review, you'll understand what's going on.
sentences.zh: 如果你读读另一条一星评论，你就会明白发生了什么。

sentences.en: This store is running a scam, we bought drinks in the store, and someone called the towing truck.
sentences.zh: 这家店在搞诈骗，我们在店里买了饮料，结果有人叫了拖车。

sentences.en: Never buy anything from this store.
sentences.zh: 永远别在这家店买任何东西。

sentences.en: Call 3-1-1.
Terrible and unethical.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕且不道德了。

sentences.en: Take your car hostage and get $150 from you.
sentences.zh: 把你的车扣为人质，然后从你身上敲诈150美元。

sentences.en: I'm Delaney Hall, and this is Service Request from 99% Invisible and Campside Media.
sentences.zh: 我是德莱尼·霍尔（Delaney Hall），这是来自《99%无形》（99% Invisible）和Campside Media的《服务请求》（Service Request）。

sentences.en: We take your burning questions about infrastructure, and we investigate.
sentences.zh: 我们收集你们关于基础设施的棘手问题，并进行调查。

sentences.en: Kelly eventually got her car back that night, and we will get into that.
sentences.zh: 凯莉那天晚上最终找回了她的车，我们稍后会详细讲。

sentences.en: But the whole experience left her with a question that she could not shake.
sentences.zh: 但整个经历给她留下了一个挥之不去的问题。

sentences.en: We're really, a whole bunch of questions.
sentences.zh: 或者说，是一连串的问题。

sentences.en: How is it that you can just park your car, 15 minutes later it's gone?
sentences.zh: 怎么会你刚把车停好，15分钟后它就不见了？

sentences.en: I don't know who's in charge of regulating this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是谁负责监管这件事。

sentences.en: I don't know who empowers these tow truck guys.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是谁赋予了这些拖车人员权力。

sentences.en: Under whose authority are they working?
sentences.zh: 他们是在谁的授权下工作的？

sentences.en: It just feels like this black box of mystery that's affecting clearly a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像一个神秘的黑箱，显然影响了很多人，

sentences.en: if the Google reviews are to be believed.
sentences.zh: 如果谷歌评论可信的话。

sentences.en: Today, the black box of mystery of towing and impoundment.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来揭开拖车和扣车行业的神秘黑箱。

sentences.en: Who decides when your car gets taken?
sentences.zh: 谁决定你的车什么时候被拖走？

sentences.en: Who decides where it goes?
sentences.zh: 谁决定它被拖到哪里？

sentences.en: And when things go wrong, which it turns out they do a lot, why is it so hard to fix?
sentences.zh: 当事情出错时——事实证明这种情况经常发生——为什么解决起来这么难？

sentences.en: When we started trying to find the answer to Kelly's question,
sentences.zh: 当我们开始试图寻找凯莉问题的答案时，

sentences.en: I learned the term that describes this kind of practice.
sentences.zh: 我学到了一个描述这种做法的术语。

sentences.en: It's called predatory towing, and it describes towers who actively hunt for cars to pick up
sentences.zh: 这叫“掠夺性拖车”，它描述的是那些主动寻找车辆进行拖走，

sentences.en: and then demand inflated fees when owners try to get them back.
sentences.zh: 然后在车主试图赎回时索要高额费用的拖车公司。

sentences.en: Predatory towing happens everywhere, but in some places it happens a lot.
sentences.zh: 掠夺性拖车到处都有，但在某些地方非常普遍。

sentences.en: Detroit, Michigan has a well-documented and long-running predatory towing problem,
sentences.zh: 密歇根州底特律有一个记录在案且长期存在的掠夺性拖车问题，

sentences.en: and so that makes it a good case study for us.
sentences.zh: 这使它成为我们研究的一个很好的案例。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a big business.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一门大生意。

sentences.en: It's a multimillion-dollar business, and they make a lot of money doing this.
sentences.zh: 这是一门价值数百万美元的生意，他们靠这个赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's why they do it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他们这么做的原因。

sentences.en: This is Tom Berry.
sentences.zh: 这位是汤姆·贝里（Tom Berry）。

sentences.en: He spent 35 years as a police officer in Detroit, and he retired as a lieutenant about a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 他在底特律当了35年警察，大约十年前以中尉身份退休。

sentences.en: Since then, he's worked as a fraud investigator for insurance companies,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他一直担任保险公司的欺诈调查员，

sentences.en: and he has seen the towing industry from basically every angle.
sentences.zh: 他基本上从各个角度审视过拖车行业。

sentences.en: He's been a cop who called tow trucks,
sentences.zh: 他曾是呼叫拖车的警察，

sentences.en: and he's been an investigator who's uncovered how corrupt towing companies actually operate.
sentences.zh: 也曾是揭露腐败拖车公司实际运作方式的调查员。

sentences.en: I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。

sentences.en: Can you help us understand, in an ideal world, how is towing supposed to be a public good?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我们理解一下，在理想情况下，拖车服务应该如何成为一种公共福利吗？

sentences.en: What kind of service do towers provide when they're working well?
sentences.zh: 当拖车公司运作良好时，他们提供什么样的服务？

sentences.en: Well, if it's working good, which we all like to see,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果运作良好，也就是我们都乐于见到的情况，

sentences.en: you live on, you know, Elm Avenue, and you come out one day,
sentences.zh: 你住在榆树大道（Elm Avenue），有一天你出来，

sentences.en: and you can't get out of your driveway because somebody's parked there.
sentences.zh: 却发现车道被堵住了，因为有人把车停在那儿。

sentences.en: So, of course, you call the police because you've got to go to work,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，你会报警，因为你得去上班，

sentences.en: and the police call the tow truck, and the tow truck comes out and moves that car out of your way
sentences.zh: 警察叫来拖车，拖车过来把那辆车移走，

sentences.en: so you can go about your business.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以去忙你的事了。

sentences.en: That's a good deal.
sentences.zh: 那是一笔好交易。

sentences.en: Also, we have accidents.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有交通事故。

sentences.en: You know, once they take care of the injured, we need to remove those cars from the road.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一旦他们处理好伤者，我们就需要把那些车从路上移走。

sentences.en: The tow companies take them to a tow yard.
sentences.zh: 拖车公司会把它们拖到拖车场。

sentences.en: In many cities, when there's a crash that needs to be cleared or a vehicle that's been abandoned on the street,
sentences.zh: 在许多城市，当发生需要清理的事故或车辆被遗弃在街上时，

sentences.en: police will call a private towing company to haul it away.
sentences.zh: 警察会叫私人拖车公司把它拖走。

sentences.en: That's how it works in Detroit, too.
sentences.zh: 底特律也是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Tom says that when he was a police officer,
sentences.zh: 汤姆说，当他还是警察时，

sentences.en: the department gave him a list of the tow companies that he was allowed to call.
sentences.zh: 警察局会给他一份允许呼叫的拖车公司名单。

sentences.en: These were companies that had a contract with the police to cover a certain area of the city.
sentences.zh: 这些公司与警方签有合同，负责覆盖城市的特定区域。

sentences.en: And most officers would go down the approved list,
sentences.zh: 大多数警察会按照批准的名单顺序呼叫，

sentences.en: calling companies until one was available to send a tow truck.
sentences.zh: 直到有一家公司有空派拖车过来。

sentences.en: But years later, as a lieutenant,
sentences.zh: 但多年后，作为中尉，

sentences.en: Tom discovered that not all police officers were doing it that way.
sentences.zh: 汤姆发现并非所有警察都这样做。

sentences.en: They were using a certain tower.
sentences.zh: 他们在使用特定的拖车公司。

sentences.en: They weren't calling the scheduled towers, the towers on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 他们没有呼叫预定的拖车公司，也就是名单上的那些。

sentences.en: They were calling their friend.
sentences.zh: 他们呼叫的是他们的朋友。

sentences.en: Some cops were calling tow companies they had a relationship with.
sentences.zh: 一些警察呼叫的是他们有私交的拖车公司。

sentences.en: And many of those companies were inflating their fees way beyond what a typical tow would coSt.
sentences.zh: 而其中许多公司会将费用抬高到远超正常拖车费用的水平。

sentences.en: Then they'd pay kickbacks to the police officers who sent the business their way.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会给把生意介绍给他们的警察支付回扣。

sentences.en: And the corruption kind of swelled.
sentences.zh: 腐败就这样膨胀起来了。

sentences.en: It just keeps surmounting.
sentences.zh: 它不断地累积。

sentences.en: And eventually, you know, it comes crashing down.
sentences.zh: 最终，你知道，它会崩塌。

sentences.en: That's what happened here in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 这就是底特律发生的事情。

sentences.en: Eventually, there was a federal investigation into the corruption that Tom is talking about.
sentences.zh: 最终，针对汤姆所说的腐败问题，联邦政府进行了调查。

sentences.en: And some cops went to jail.
sentences.zh: 一些警察进了监狱。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the end of towing problems in the city.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是该市拖车问题的终结。

sentences.en: In fact, Tom says some of the most problematic towing doesn't even involve the police.
sentences.zh: 事实上，汤姆说，一些最严重的问题甚至不涉及警察。

sentences.en: It involves situations like Kelly's, where people get towed for parking in a private lot.
sentences.zh: 它涉及像凯莉那样的情况，人们因为把车停在私人停车场而被拖走。

sentences.en: I'm curious if, kind of zooming out, you can walk me through how a predatory towing operation works.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，如果把视野放宽，你能带我了解一下掠夺性拖车是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Like, what does a typical day look like?
sentences.zh: 比如，典型的一天是什么样的？

sentences.en: What are the most common schemes that you see?
sentences.zh: 你见过最常见的套路是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think that most towers are basically honeSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为大多数拖车人员基本上是诚实的。

sentences.en: First, I want to give them a little accolade.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想给他们一点赞许。

sentences.en: But so what happens, like your friend there at the 7-Eleven, so it's illegal to park in private property and go to the doctor's office, let's say, or go, you know,
sentences.zh: 但事情是这样的，就像你那位在7-Eleven的朋友，在私人领地停车然后去医生办公室，或者去，你知道，

sentences.en: go do your shopping.
sentences.zh: 去购物，这是违法的。

sentences.en: So if you own a business in your city, you know, McDonald's or Burger King or whatever, and you have private citizens that aren't patronizing your business, tying up your lot,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在城里经营一家企业，比如麦当劳或汉堡王之类的，而有私人车主不去消费却占用了你的车位，

sentences.en: and they keep coming in there and you're losing customers because your lot's full of people going to shop at Macy's, then you're mad.
sentences.zh: 他们不断地停在那里，而你因为停车场被那些去梅西百货购物的人占满而流失了顾客，那你就会很生气。

sentences.en: Yeah, so you, the business owner, can contact, you know, Joe's Towing and say, hey, I got a red Chevy out in my lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以你，企业主，可以联系，比如“乔氏拖车”（Joe's Towing）说，嘿，我停车场里有一辆红色雪佛兰。

sentences.en: Can you come and get it?
sentences.zh: 你能过来把它拖走吗？

sentences.en: It's been here for a half hour.
sentences.zh: 它已经停了半小时了。

sentences.en: This practice makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这种做法是有道理的。

sentences.en: A business needs to keep its lot clear for actual customers.
sentences.zh: 企业需要保持停车场空出，留给真正的顾客。

sentences.en: And that's what happened to Kelly.
sentences.zh: 而这就是凯莉遇到的情况。

sentences.en: She parked at a 7-Eleven, walked to a neighboring restaurant, and then came back to find her car gone.
sentences.zh: 她把车停在7-Eleven，走到隔壁餐馆，回来时发现车不见了。

sentences.en: She technically broke the rules, and the tow company had the right to take her car.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，她违反了规定，拖车公司有权拖走她的车。

sentences.en: But there are sketchier tactics that some towers use to maximize the number of cars they can grab.
sentences.zh: 但有些拖车公司会使用更阴险的手段来最大化他们能拖走的车辆数量。

sentences.en: For instance, spotters.
sentences.zh: 例如，安排“盯梢者”。

sentences.en: Spotters are paid citizens that live in that area.
sentences.zh: 盯梢者是居住在该地区的有偿市民。

sentences.en: I approach them and say, hey, I'm the owner of Joe's Towing, and I know that your apartment overlooks, you know, the Burger King lot over here.
sentences.zh: 我接近他们说，嘿，我是乔氏拖车的车主，我知道你的公寓俯瞰着这边的汉堡王停车场。

sentences.en: So we meet and say, okay, here's what I want you to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们见面说，好吧，我要你做的是：

sentences.en: I want you to watch this lot.
sentences.zh: 我要你盯着这个停车场。

sentences.en: And if you see somebody go into that lot and not use the business, you call me.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到有人把车停进去却不去消费，你就给我打电话。

sentences.en: And so I'll be right there.
sentences.zh: 然后我马上就会赶到。

sentences.en: And if I get the tow job, you get 50 or 100 bucks.
sentences.zh: 如果我接到了拖车生意，你就拿50或100美元。

sentences.en: So tow truck makes cash.
sentences.zh: 所以拖车公司赚了现金。

sentences.en: People make 50 bucks, no taxes.
sentences.zh: 这些人赚了50美元，不用交税。

sentences.en: Everybody's happy except the person that parked there.
sentences.zh: 除了那个停车的人，大家都很高兴。

sentences.en: Except the person who parked there.
sentences.zh: 除了那个停车的人。

sentences.en: So this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: Tow companies, they basically recruit a neighborhood network of eyes on the ground, of spies.
sentences.zh: 拖车公司基本上是在社区里招募了一张眼线网，也就是间谍。

sentences.en: That's a good way to put it, a neighborhood network.
sentences.zh: 这话说得好，就像一个社区网络。

sentences.en: Excellent.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: People who are just keeping an eye on these various parking lots.
sentences.zh: 这些人专门盯着这些各式各样的停车场。

sentences.en: And when they see someone parked there and not use the business, they just give the tow truck driver a call and they get a kickback.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到有人把车停在那儿却不去消费时，就会给拖车司机打电话，然后他们能从中拿回扣。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In some cities, it's illegal for tow companies to use spotters.
sentences.zh: 在一些城市，拖车公司使用“盯梢员”是违法的。

sentences.en: But not in New York City or in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 但在纽约市或底特律却不是。

sentences.en: One tow company there became so notorious for using spotters, they felt the need to put out this little explainer video on their Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 底特律有一家拖车公司因为使用盯梢员而臭名昭著，他们甚至觉得有必要在Facebook主页上发布这段简短的解释视频。

sentences.en: A lot of people think a spotter is illegal, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为使用盯梢员是非法的，但其实不是。

sentences.en: There's nothing illegal about it.
sentences.zh: 这完全合法。

sentences.en: They're just maintaining parking spaces for the property owner.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在为业主维护停车位。

sentences.en: After the break, we'll talk with a driver who used to work for that notorious Detroit tow company.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将采访一位曾经在那家臭名昭著的底特律拖车公司工作过的司机。

sentences.en: Well, I guess to start, could you just introduce yourself, like your name and where you are and what you're doing?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想先请你做个自我介绍，比如你的名字、你现在在哪儿，以及你在做什么？

sentences.en: My name is Shane Nation.
sentences.zh: 我叫谢恩·内申。

sentences.en: I'm in Detroit, Michigan, and I currently tow, and I've been in the industry for about five years.
sentences.zh: 我在密歇根州底特律，目前从事拖车工作，在这个行业干了大约五年了。

sentences.en: When I spoke with Shane, he was in his tow truck between calls on his lunch break.
sentences.zh: 我和谢恩交谈时，他正坐在午休时间的拖车里，等待下一个任务。

sentences.en: As far as I can tell, there aren't a lot of tow truck drivers who are willing to talk with a journalist about the realities of the job.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，没多少拖车司机愿意和记者谈论这份工作的真相。

sentences.en: But Shane is one of them.
sentences.zh: 但谢恩是其中之一。

sentences.en: He started in the industry when he was just 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 他16岁时就入行了。

sentences.en: Once I started working in the industry, it's like a bug.
sentences.zh: 一旦开始干这一行，就像上瘾了一样。

sentences.en: It's very hard to go do something where you're not as free, like go sit in an office or inside all day long.
sentences.zh: 很难再去干那种没那么自由的工作，比如整天坐在办公室里。

sentences.en: Honestly, it's not boring.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这工作一点也不无聊。

sentences.en: There's people that have been towing for 25 years, and they'll tell you that they learn new stuff every day because it's just genuinely that type of job.
sentences.zh: 有些干了25年的拖车司机也会告诉你，他们每天都能学到新东西，因为这行确实就是这样。

sentences.en: So for people who are not familiar with towing, what is a typical day like in the life of a tow truck driver?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于不了解拖车行业的人来说，拖车司机的典型一天是怎样的？

sentences.en: You normally sit in the truck, you play on your phone, do whatever to let time pass, and then you just wait for police calls to come in.
sentences.zh: 通常就是坐在车里，玩玩手机，打发时间，然后等着警方的电话。

sentences.en: Those could look like impounds, like somebody got arrested, and we would tow their car to an impound lot.
sentences.zh: 任务可能是扣车，比如有人被捕了，我们就得把他们的车拖到扣车场。

sentences.en: It could look like a car crash, and we have to be out there cleaning the scene on the highway or something.
sentences.zh: 也可能是车祸现场，我们得去高速公路上清理现场之类的。

sentences.en: And it could be as simple as your mom broke down, and she just needs a tow to the mechanic shop to get her car fixed.
sentences.zh: 也可能很简单，比如你妈妈的车坏了，需要拖到修理厂去修。

sentences.en: Have you towed your mom?
sentences.zh: 你拖过你妈妈的车吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, not my mother.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是我妈。

sentences.en: Luckily, she buys newer vehicles and gets warranties and stuff, but family members, yes.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，她买的都是新车，有保修之类的，但其他家庭成员的车我拖过。

sentences.en: So they're like, oh, I know exactly who to call.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会说，哦，我知道该找谁了。

sentences.en: Shane.
sentences.zh: 谢恩。

sentences.en: Yeah, unfortunately, that is what seems to be what they do.
sentences.zh: 是啊，不幸的是，他们好像就是这么做的。

sentences.en: Shane's first real towing job was with a company in Detroit that had a reputation for predatory towing.
sentences.zh: 谢恩的第一份正式拖车工作是在底特律一家以掠夺性拖车闻名的公司。

sentences.en: Shane doesn't actually have a problem naming this company.
sentences.zh: 谢恩其实并不介意说出这家公司的名字。

sentences.en: He's spoken on TV in Detroit about them.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在底特律的电视节目上谈论过他们。

sentences.en: But we don't want to name them in this episode.
sentences.zh: 但我们不想在这一集里指名道姓。

sentences.en: We don't want Shane to get in trouble.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让谢恩惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: So since day one there, they would say, hey, look, we're on the news all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以从第一天起，他们就会说，嘿，你看，我们经常上新闻。

sentences.en: It is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: People don't like their car getting towed.
sentences.zh: 人们不喜欢自己的车被拖走。

sentences.en: So that's pretty much how I was told there.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在那儿被告知的情况。

sentences.en: Like, hey, you're going to see that we're this, this, and that.
sentences.zh: 就像是，嘿，你会看到我们被说成这样那样。

sentences.en: And just don't believe it because, you know, we're just doing the public a service, and some people don't appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 别信那些，你知道，我们是在为公众服务，有些人不领情而已。

sentences.en: At first, Shane thought maybe that's just how the world works.
sentences.zh: 起初，谢恩以为这可能就是世界的运作方式。

sentences.en: People just complain to the media a lot.
sentences.zh: 人们总是喜欢向媒体抱怨。

sentences.en: Plus, he liked his job.
sentences.zh: 况且，他喜欢这份工作。

sentences.en: He liked the trucks and getting greasy and how every day was interesting and new.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢那些卡车，喜欢弄得满手油污，喜欢每天都充满新鲜感。

sentences.en: A lot of the jobs he was doing were private property impounds, or PPIs.
sentences.zh: 他做的很多工作都是私有财产扣车，简称PPI。

sentences.en: That's when a tow company has a contract with a property owner, like an apartment complex or a 7-Eleven, to tow cars that shouldn't be there.
sentences.zh: 也就是拖车公司与业主（比如公寓大楼或7-Eleven）签订合同，拖走不该停在那里的车。

sentences.en: And this company that Shane worked for was aggressive about it.
sentences.zh: 而谢恩工作的这家公司在这方面非常激进。

sentences.en: They would work with spotters, like the ones Tom told us about.
sentences.zh: 他们会和汤姆告诉我们的那种盯梢员合作。

sentences.en: They had people sitting in the parking lot, watching and waiting for someone to park illegally.
sentences.zh: 他们让人坐在停车场里，盯着并等待有人违规停车。

sentences.en: We had two different spotters.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个不同的盯梢员。

sentences.en: They would sit in tenant-out cars and just wait for somebody to pull up.
sentences.zh: 他们会坐在没人的车里，等着有人过来。

sentences.en: We would sit around the corner.
sentences.zh: 我们就坐在拐角处。

sentences.en: We wouldn't be no further than five minutes away.
sentences.zh: 离得绝对不会超过五分钟路程。

sentences.en: One of the lots Shane worked was across the street from the Med Center, which is a cluster of major hospitals in downtown Detroit.
sentences.zh: 谢恩工作过的一个停车场就在医疗中心对面，那是底特律市中心的一片大型医院群。

sentences.en: People would park in the apartment complex lot and then walk across the street to visit someone in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 人们会把车停在公寓大楼的停车场，然后步行穿过马路去医院探望病人。

sentences.en: And Shane's job was to tow their cars the moment they walked away.
sentences.zh: 而谢恩的工作就是在他们走开的那一刻把车拖走。

sentences.en: We'd pull up right away, grab their car, and drive off with it.
sentences.zh: 我们马上开过去，钩住他们的车，然后直接开走。

sentences.en: Now, these people, sometimes they would come out and, you know, they'd be screaming, yelling,
sentences.zh: 这些人有时会跑出来，你知道，他们会尖叫、大喊：

sentences.en: I don't have another car.
sentences.zh: 我没有别的车了。

sentences.en: How am I supposed to get to work?
sentences.zh: 我怎么去上班？

sentences.en: How am I supposed to take my kids to school?
sentences.zh: 我怎么送孩子上学？

sentences.en: And when I was 17, I'm not going to lie, I had no remorse for them.
sentences.zh: 我17岁的时候，说实话，我一点也不觉得愧疚。

sentences.en: I didn't feel bad for them at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不为他们感到难过。

sentences.en: But once I started getting older and having bills to pay and understanding that it's genuinely hard out here in the world to survive,
sentences.zh: 但随着我年龄增长，有了账单要付，也明白了在这个世界上生存确实很难，

sentences.en: especially on a low income, and then somebody's come in and taken your car when you're just trying to visit, you know,
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于低收入人群来说，当你只是想去医院探望父母时，却有人把你的车拖走了，

sentences.en: your mom or your dad that's in the hospital, I can understand now that's like just a really crappy thing to do to somebody.
sentences.zh: 我现在能理解那对别人来说真的是一件非常糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Shane says he would sometimes spend whole shifts sitting in his truck near that one parking lot waiting for spotters to call in tows.
sentences.zh: 谢恩说，他有时会整个班次都坐在那个停车场附近的卡车里，等着盯梢员打电话来通知拖车。

sentences.en: Because that single lot was sort of a goldmine.
sentences.zh: 因为那个停车场简直是个金矿。

sentences.en: It's 100% returns other than the fuel you used on profits.
sentences.zh: 除了油费，利润率是百分之百。

sentences.en: So, I mean, they're making a killing just towing 15 to 20 cars a day off that one lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他们光靠在那一个停车场每天拖走15到20辆车就赚翻了。

sentences.en: And they have all of downtown Detroit.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还承包了整个底特律市中心。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's a big operation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这规模很大。

sentences.en: Given the company's reputation, sometimes the Detroit police would show up to see what was going on.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这家公司的名声，有时底特律警方会过来看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: Or they'd respond to complaints from people who were getting their cars towed.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会回应那些车被拖走的人的投诉。

sentences.en: But the company was ready for that.
sentences.zh: 但公司对此早有准备。

sentences.en: Shane says they trained their employees on what to say when the police arrived,
sentences.zh: 谢恩说，他们会培训员工在警察到达时该说什么，

sentences.en: which laws to mention in their arguments for towing a certain car.
sentences.zh: 在争论拖车合法性时该引用哪些法律。

sentences.en: Shane's interactions with the public weren't any better.
sentences.zh: 谢恩与公众的互动也好不到哪儿去。

sentences.en: It was all so confrontational.
sentences.zh: 一切都充满了对抗。

sentences.en: They would always beg and plead.
sentences.zh: 他们总是乞求和哀求。

sentences.en: And that's understandable, especially if you don't have the money.
sentences.zh: 这可以理解，尤其是如果你没钱的话。

sentences.en: It was standard.
sentences.zh: 这都是常态。

sentences.en: I was constantly, for lack of a better word, I was constantly the a-hole in every predicament I've ever,
sentences.zh: 我一直，用个不恰当的词，我在每一次困境中都是那个混蛋，

sentences.en: like every interaction I had, I was the aggressor.
sentences.zh: 就像我经历的每一次互动，我都是那个侵略者。

sentences.en: If you think about it, it is kind of wild that these non-law enforcement private companies are allowed to just take people's unattended vehicles.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这些非执法的私人公司被允许直接拖走人们无人看管的车辆，确实有点疯狂。

sentences.en: Shane says that bad practices are common in the world of private property impounds because there are basically no checks in the system.
sentences.zh: 谢恩说，私有财产扣车领域普遍存在不良做法，因为系统中基本上没有任何制衡。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It's the least regulated.
sentences.zh: 这是监管最薄弱的领域。

sentences.en: You're not pulling up on a police scene with police there.
sentences.zh: 你不是在警察在场的执法现场执行任务。

sentences.en: And you're not pulling up on a broken down vehicle with the car's owner there.
sentences.zh: 也不是在车主在场的车辆抛锚现场。

sentences.en: You're pulling up on an unattended vehicle that you have full access to.
sentences.zh: 你面对的是一辆你可以完全掌控的无人看管车辆。

sentences.en: And, I mean, you just hook up this car and you call the police nearby and you go,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你只需要钩住这辆车，给附近的警察打个电话说：

sentences.en: hey, I'm towing this car because it's parked incorrectly on this lot.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我正在拖走这辆车，因为它在这个停车场违规停放。

sentences.en: There's no verification of this whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 这完全没有任何核实过程。

sentences.en: You just, you call the police and you tell them you're doing it and they put the car in lien so it can't be reported stolen.
sentences.zh: 你只需要给警察打电话告知一声，他们就会把车登记在案，这样就不会被报为失窃车辆了。

sentences.en: That's all it is to PPIs and there's just no verification in the system.
sentences.zh: PPI就是这么回事，系统中根本没有核实机制。

sentences.en: So everybody exploits it.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都在钻空子。

sentences.en: So you're doing this at this apartment complex lot.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那个公寓大楼的停车场做这些事。

sentences.en: You've gotten a little older.
sentences.zh: 你年纪大了一点。

sentences.en: You're like, this doesn't feel good because you understand kind of the implications of having your car towed.
sentences.zh: 你觉得这感觉不好，因为你开始明白车被拖走意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's expensive.
sentences.zh: 这很贵。

sentences.en: It's like a huge headache.
sentences.zh: 这简直是个巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: So what happened from there?
sentences.zh: 那后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So it was never that, like, I wanted to continue doing it.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过要继续做下去。

sentences.en: It was kind of the fact that I had bills to pay and my own family to feed is why I stayed there for so much longer after that time period.
sentences.zh: 只是因为我有账单要付，还要养活自己的家人，所以我才在那之后又多待了那么久。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 明白。

sentences.en: But, yeah, like, I hated it every day after that.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，在那之后我每天都痛恨这份工作。

sentences.en: Like, it made me lose my love for towing and it, I genuinely just wanted out in any way, shape or form by the end of it.
sentences.zh: 它让我失去了对拖车工作的热爱，到最后，我真的只想以任何方式离开。

sentences.en: Shane was having a full-blown crisis of conscience.
sentences.zh: 谢恩经历了一场彻底的良心危机。

sentences.en: He dreaded going to work and spending all day towing people who he believed didn't really deserve it.
sentences.zh: 他害怕去上班，害怕整天拖走那些他认为并不该被拖走的车。

sentences.en: Eventually, he left the predatory tow company.
sentences.zh: 最终，他离开了那家掠夺性拖车公司。

sentences.en: He thought he might go back to working in fast food.
sentences.zh: 他想过回去做快餐工作。

sentences.en: But instead, he started with a different company where he was doing different kinds of tows.
sentences.zh: 但相反，他去了另一家公司，开始做不同类型的拖车工作。

sentences.en: I just didn't want to do PPIs.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想再做PPI了。

sentences.en: That was my biggest thing was private property impounds feel like they're just not necessary, like, at least in the way they did it.
sentences.zh: 我最大的心结就是觉得私有财产扣车根本没必要，至少他们那种做法没必要。

sentences.en: Like, it was just unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 就像，那完全是多此一举。

sentences.en: And I just, I did them so much 24-7 that I just didn't want to do them ever again.
sentences.zh: 我之前没日没夜地做这些，真的再也不想做了。

sentences.en: And that was my main thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的主要想法。

sentences.en: Where I'm at now, all I do is services.
sentences.zh: 我现在做的工作全是服务性质的。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not towing anybody's car because I want to.
sentences.zh: 我不会因为想拖车就去拖别人的车。

sentences.en: You know, it's simply they call or the police call.
sentences.zh: 你知道，都是他们打电话或者警察打电话。

sentences.en: And I'm going there to either clean up the wreck or I'm going there to get those people home.
sentences.zh: 我去那里要么是清理事故现场，要么是帮那些人把车送回家。

sentences.en: And especially where I'm at now, it's never the case that I'm going there for any other reason other than to service them.
sentences.zh: 特别是我现在所在的地方，我去那里从来都是为了提供服务，没有其他原因。

sentences.en: These conversations with Tom and Shane helped me understand so much better what might have happened with Kelly's car.
sentences.zh: 这些与汤姆和谢恩的对话让我更好地理解了凯莉的车可能发生了什么。

sentences.en: She was involved in a private property impound situation.
sentences.zh: 她卷入了一起私有财产扣车事件。

sentences.en: She parked at that 7-Eleven illegally.
sentences.zh: 她把车违规停在了那家7-Eleven。

sentences.en: There may have been a spotter that saw her do it.
sentences.zh: 可能有一个盯梢员看到了她违规停车。

sentences.en: And the company probably had a relationship with a toer who was contacted as soon as she walked away.
sentences.zh: 而且该公司可能与某个拖车司机有合作关系，她一走开就联系了对方。

sentences.en: So after standing in the parking lot trying to figure out what to do, she and her friends decided to call the tow company.
sentences.zh: 所以在停车场站着不知所措后，她和朋友决定给拖车公司打电话。

sentences.en: So we called the number and we actually had to call, like, multiple times to get the information we needed.
sentences.zh: 我们打了那个电话，实际上我们不得不打好几次才能得到我们需要的信息。

sentences.en: Because, like, we'd call and then they would hang up.
sentences.zh: 因为我们打过去，他们就会挂断。

sentences.en: Or we'd call and sort of not get the right information.
sentences.zh: 或者我们打过去，却得不到正确的信息。

sentences.en: At one point, Kelly asked the tow company to confirm that they had her car by reading back the license plate number.
sentences.zh: 有一次，凯莉要求拖车公司通过读出车牌号来确认他们扣留了她的车。

sentences.en: And they're like, we can't give you the license plate.
sentences.zh: 他们却说，我们不能告诉你车牌号。

sentences.en: And at one point, they were like, yeah, we have your car, but come back tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，他们说，是的，我们有你的车，但明天再来吧。

sentences.en: It was all extremely confusing.
sentences.zh: 这一切都极其令人困惑。

sentences.en: But eventually, Kelly took a cab home to let her dog out for a walk.
sentences.zh: 但最终，凯莉打车回家去遛狗了。

sentences.en: And her friends decided to go get the car themselves.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友们决定自己去取车。

sentences.en: The impound lot was about a mile from the 7-Eleven, and they had to walk there.
sentences.zh: 扣车场离那家7-Eleven大约一英里，他们不得不走过去。

sentences.en: They eventually found the place.
sentences.zh: 他们最终找到了那个地方。

sentences.en: And through the holes in the front gate, they could see Kelly's car.
sentences.zh: 透过前门的缝隙，他们看到了凯莉的车。

sentences.en: They got there, and there was a building that was brightly lit up inside, indicating that perhaps the office was not actually closed.
sentences.zh: 他们到了那里，发现里面有一栋建筑灯火通明，说明办公室可能并没有关门。

sentences.en: But they were brought into this building, and the guy was like, it's going to be $350 to get your car back because the office is closed right now.
sentences.zh: 但他们被带进那栋建筑后，那个人说，取车要350美元，因为现在办公室已经下班了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially, I'm pretty sure the sign said $125.
sentences.zh: 是啊，尤其是，我非常确定牌子上写的是125美元。

sentences.en: Like, the sign had a pay scale on there, and he was immediately like, that's going to be $350.
sentences.zh: 牌子上标有收费标准，但他立刻就说，那得要350美元。

sentences.en: So there's sort of this, there's this negotiation going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，这中间存在某种……某种谈判。

sentences.en: It's like.
sentences.zh: 就像是。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全是这样。

sentences.en: There's totally a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 确实存在谈判。

sentences.en: And it included, like, at first they said, oh, because I'm not physically there, that's an extra fee.
sentences.zh: 而且还包括，起初他们说，哦，因为我人不在现场，所以要额外收费。

sentences.en: And then they said, oh, the business is closed, it's after hours, so that's another fee.
sentences.zh: 然后他们又说，哦，公司下班了，现在是营业时间外，所以又要收一笔钱。

sentences.en: But there wasn't actually a fee structure.
sentences.zh: 但实际上根本没有收费结构。

sentences.en: It was just, like, a negotiation, like a bartering.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹就是一种谈判，就像以物易物一样。

sentences.en: They were just making it up.
sentences.zh: 他们完全是信口开河。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They kidnapped my car and then, like, ransomed it for an uncertain amount of money based on how much cash my friends had on hand.
sentences.zh: 他们绑架了我的车，然后像勒索赎金一样，根据我朋友手头有多少现金来决定要多少钱。

sentences.en: Like, it's crazy they can do that.
sentences.zh: 他们能这么做真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But according to Tom, the retired cop, tow companies do this all the time.
sentences.zh: 但据退休警察Tom说，拖车公司经常这么干。

sentences.en: They pretend they're closed so that people have to come back the next day, and that allows them to inflate the storage fees they charge.
sentences.zh: 他们假装下班了，这样人们就得第二天再来，而这让他们有机会抬高收取的保管费。

sentences.en: They demand to see registration and insurance, which is often in the car that's been impounded.
sentences.zh: 他们要求查看车辆登记证和保险单，而这些文件通常都在被扣押的车里。

sentences.en: And so people have to run around gathering new documents.
sentences.zh: 所以人们不得不四处奔波去补办文件。

sentences.en: It might take them a day, it might take them two days to go get that information and bring it back to satisfy the tow company.
sentences.zh: 可能需要一天，也可能需要两天才能拿到这些信息并带回来，以满足拖车公司的要求。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, another $50 a day, another $50 a day for keeping your car.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，每天又要多收50美元，每天50美元的保管费。

sentences.en: Often, these businesses don't disclose their fee structures.
sentences.zh: 通常，这些公司不会公开他们的收费结构。

sentences.en: And even when they do, the fees can be manipulated.
sentences.zh: 即使公开了，费用也可能被操纵。

sentences.en: So, well, it came in on the 2nd at 11 o'clock at night, and here it is the 3rd, and it's 1 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 所以，车是2号晚上11点进来的，现在是3号凌晨1点。

sentences.en: Well, that's a 2-day storage, that's $110.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这算保管了两天，要收110美元。

sentences.en: Well, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: My car's only been here for two hours.
sentences.zh: 我的车才在这儿停了两个小时。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's the way it is.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但规矩就是这样。

sentences.en: Because it's technically touched two days, even if it was just a few hours in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 因为从技术上讲，这跨了两天，哪怕只是半夜里的几个小时。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Kelly's friends were lucky, if you can call it that, because they showed up that same night.
sentences.zh: Kelly的朋友们还算幸运——如果这也能叫幸运的话——因为他们当天晚上就赶到了。

sentences.en: They eventually paid $200 to get the car back.
sentences.zh: 他们最终付了200美元才把车赎回来。

sentences.en: It's really, really sketchy.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常、非常可疑。

sentences.en: Like, none of this feels legal.
sentences.zh: 感觉这一切都不合法。

sentences.en: You can just take someone's car, ransom it, figure out an amount of money between you.
sentences.zh: 你居然可以直接把别人的车拖走，勒索赎金，然后双方商量出一个金额。

sentences.en: And then they said, no receipt.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还说，不给收据。

sentences.en: So they just had to pay their $200.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只能付那200美元。

sentences.en: How else are you going to get your car back?
sentences.zh: 不然你还能怎么把车拿回来？

sentences.en: Like, these five guys have it.
sentences.zh: 毕竟那五个家伙扣着车呢。

sentences.en: What else are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 你还能怎么办？

sentences.en: It almost seems like the towers don't want you to get your car back.
sentences.zh: 看起来拖车公司甚至不希望你把车赎回去。

sentences.en: Or, at the very least, they might not mind if you don't retrieve your car.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，如果你不去赎车，他们可能也无所谓。

sentences.en: Well, what some of these tow companies do, they know good cars and bad cars.
sentences.zh: 有些拖车公司会这么做，他们能分清哪些是好车，哪些是烂车。

sentences.en: You know what I mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你知道我这话是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, hey, that's an older car, but it's got good treads on it, good struts.
sentences.zh: 比如，嘿，那辆车虽然旧，但轮胎花纹好，减震器也不错。

sentences.en: You know, it looks pretty okay.
sentences.zh: 看起来还挺好的。

sentences.en: I could probably get some money for that.
sentences.zh: 我大概能卖个好价钱。

sentences.en: So they kind of pull that to the side of the auction that they have every 30 days.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会把车挪到每30天举行一次的拍卖会那边。

sentences.en: Cars are valuable.
sentences.zh: 车是有价值的。

sentences.en: So this is another way they're making money.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们赚钱的另一种方式。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They hold a person's car until the fees are so high, the person can't afford to retrieve it.
sentences.zh: 他们扣着人的车，直到费用高到车主赎不回来为止。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And then they sell that car at auction, scrap it for parts, make money on the car itself.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就把车拿去拍卖，或者拆解卖零件，从车本身赚钱。

sentences.en: That's why it's a multi-million dollar business, towing us.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么拖车行业是一个价值数百万美元的生意。

sentences.en: And people don't realize that.
sentences.zh: 人们并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: For that reason, Tom says bad towers might target cars that look a little bit junky or old, like Kelly's 2011 Mazda.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，Tom说那些不良拖车公司可能会专门针对看起来破旧一点的车，比如Kelly那辆2011年的马自达。

sentences.en: Cars that look like they might be underinsured, or their owners might not have hundreds of dollars on hand to get them back.
sentences.zh: 那些看起来保险不足，或者车主手头拿不出几百美元赎车的车。

sentences.en: Because they're easy targets.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是容易下手的目标。

sentences.en: And generally, those owners of those cars don't squeak.
sentences.zh: 而且通常，这些车主也不会声张。

sentences.en: They don't make complaints.
sentences.zh: 他们不会去投诉。

sentences.en: I don't know if that's their reasoning, but it sounds reasonable to me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否是他们的逻辑，但这听起来确实有道理。

sentences.en: We, you know, go after the low-hanging fruit versus the high-hanging fruit.
sentences.zh: 我们，你知道，专挑软柿子捏，而不是去碰硬骨头。

sentences.en: Towers can get away with this in part because there's very little oversight.
sentences.zh: 拖车公司之所以能逍遥法外，部分原因是监管太少。

sentences.en: The towing industry is regulated by a patchwork of laws across the country.
sentences.zh: 拖车行业受全国各地各种零散法律的监管。

sentences.en: They vary state by state.
sentences.zh: 各州的情况各不相同。

sentences.en: According to research done by a consumer watchdog group, only about half of states set a cap on towing or impoundment fees.
sentences.zh: 根据消费者监督组织的研究，只有大约一半的州对拖车费或扣车费设定了上限。

sentences.en: More than 30 states don't require rates to be displayed or disclosed.
sentences.zh: 超过30个州不要求公示或披露收费标准。

sentences.en: 13 states don't even require the towing company to notify you that your car has been towed.
sentences.zh: 13个州甚至不要求拖车公司通知你车被拖走了。

sentences.en: And in 34 states, kickbacks are legal.
sentences.zh: 而在34个州，回扣是合法的。

sentences.en: All of which creates a massive gray area.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都造成了一个巨大的灰色地带。

sentences.en: Some of what they do just sounds like aggressive business practices.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的一些事听起来只是激进的商业行为。

sentences.en: You know, like towing companies, working hard, working proactively to tow illegally parked cars and to make money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像拖车公司努力工作，积极主动地拖走违停车辆来赚钱一样。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm wondering, when do you think it crosses the line from, you know, going hard for business to something more like fraud?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你认为什么时候这种行为会越界，从努力做生意变成欺诈？

sentences.en: You know, I don't know where the line is, but there's certainly a wavy line there that nobody knows about.
sentences.zh: 我不知道界限在哪里，但那里确实有一条模糊的界限，没人知道它在哪。

sentences.en: But it's interesting what you're saying, because it strikes me as part of the problem, which is that you hear about these tactics that bad towers use, and they just seem unfair.
sentences.zh: 但你说的很有意思，因为这让我觉得这就是问题的一部分，你听说了那些不良拖车公司使用的手段，它们看起来就是不公平。

sentences.en: And yet, it's not totally clear they're breaking some law.
sentences.zh: 然而，并不完全清楚他们是否触犯了法律。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: There's a big gray area there that's huge.
sentences.zh: 那里确实存在一个巨大的灰色地带。

sentences.en: So, the only way to stop it is get a law, make a law, or an ordinance in the city where you can make it, and prosecute them.
sentences.zh: 所以，阻止它的唯一方法就是立法，制定法律或城市条例，然后起诉他们。

sentences.en: And don't take your foot off the gas.
sentences.zh: 而且千万别松懈。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, many cities don't fight it until it's so out of control that now they can't get it all back in the box.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，许多城市在问题失控之前都不会去管，直到现在他们已经无法收拾残局了。

sentences.en: You know, the box has been opened, and that crap's flying all around.
sentences.zh: 你知道，潘多拉魔盒已经打开了，烂摊子到处都是。

sentences.en: How are you going to get that box closed again?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么把那个盒子重新关上？

sentences.en: You know, it's difficult, and that's what happens when you let little things, like the little tow.
sentences.zh: 这很难，这就是当你放任小事发生时会产生的结果，比如小小的拖车违规。

sentences.en: Hey, you charged your four-day stow, and you only had it one.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你明明只扣了一天，却收了四天的保管费。

sentences.en: When you do that, if you don't stop it, it's just going to be six days, seven days, because that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 当你这么做时，如果不制止，以后就会变成六天、七天，因为事情就是这样发展的。

sentences.en: That's just human nature.
sentences.zh: 这就是人性。

sentences.en: It's just going to keep growing.
sentences.zh: 它只会不断膨胀。

sentences.en: So, the only way to stop it, in my opinion, is sort of nip it in the bud.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我看来，阻止它的唯一方法就是将其扼杀在萌芽状态。

sentences.en: You know, stop it when it's small so we can control it.
sentences.zh: 在它还小的时候就制止它，这样我们才能控制住。

sentences.en: Tom's advice is to pass regulations and then crack down.
sentences.zh: Tom的建议是出台法规，然后严厉打击。

sentences.en: But some cities have tried a different approach.
sentences.zh: 但有些城市尝试了不同的方法。

sentences.en: They've just cut private towers out entirely, and they've set up their own public towing operations.
sentences.zh: 他们完全剔除了私人拖车公司，建立了属于自己的公共拖车系统。

sentences.en: But getting that going can be a heavy lift.
sentences.zh: 但要实现这一点可能非常困难。

sentences.en: It requires a city to acquire land for the impoundment lot, and trucks to do the towing, and people to staff the operation.
sentences.zh: 这需要城市征用土地作为扣车场，购买拖车，并配备工作人员来运营。

sentences.en: How common is it for a city to have their own trucks, their own lot?
sentences.zh: 城市拥有自己的拖车和停车场的情况普遍吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's common.
sentences.zh: 我不认为很普遍。

sentences.en: I think it's a rarity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很罕见。

sentences.en: And why isn't it more common?
sentences.zh: 那为什么不更普遍一些呢？

sentences.en: It's a lot.
sentences.zh: 这太麻烦了。

sentences.en: Who's going to oversee it?
sentences.zh: 谁来监管呢？

sentences.en: Are you going to have policemen oversee it?
sentences.zh: 你要让警察来监管吗？

sentences.en: There's so many cost considerations, I think, for that, that they just don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这涉及太多的成本考量，他们根本不想做。

sentences.en: They want somebody else to do it, which I would, too.
sentences.zh: 他们想让别人来做，换做是我，我也会这么想。

sentences.en: I think that's what happens with the cities, is they don't want to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 我想城市就是这样，他们不想处理这些麻烦事。

sentences.en: What's one piece of advice you have for someone whose car has just been towed?
sentences.zh: 对于车刚被拖走的人，你有什么建议？

sentences.en: Of course, it's a situation.
sentences.zh: 当然，这确实是个棘手的情况。

sentences.en: If it's legitimate, you had an accident, and the police come out in a normal city, and they're going to tow it to their yard, that's the way it should go.
sentences.zh: 如果是合法的，比如你出了事故，警察在正常的城市赶到现场，他们会把车拖到他们的停车场，这才是正常的流程。

sentences.en: If you've got insurance on your car, let it run its course.
sentences.zh: 如果你的车有保险，就按流程走。

sentences.en: First, make your claim, call your company, make an insurance claim, but be aware of, especially in parking, private property tows.
sentences.zh: 首先，提出索赔，给保险公司打电话，但要特别注意私人停车场的拖车问题。

sentences.en: It's extremely lucrative.
sentences.zh: 这非常赚钱。

sentences.en: When you pull into a lot, if you see a sign, you know, this area controlled by Tom's Towing, you know, violators will be towed.
sentences.zh: 当你驶入停车场时，如果看到牌子上写着“此区域由Tom拖车公司管理，违者将被拖走”。

sentences.en: Pay attention to those signs, because a lot of those places, they got somebody watching, and they're going to tow you.
sentences.zh: 注意那些牌子，因为很多地方都有人盯着，他们会把你拖走。

sentences.en: Be careful where you park.
sentences.zh: 停车时要小心。

sentences.en: What I hear you saying when I say, you know, what's your piece of advice?
sentences.zh: 当我问你有什么建议时，我听到的意思是……

sentences.en: It's basically, don't get towed.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，别被拖走。

sentences.en: But, like, do not get yourself caught up in this situation.
sentences.zh: 但是，千万别让自己卷入这种境地。

sentences.en: If you come out, and they got the car on the hook, okay, pay the drop fee.
sentences.zh: 如果你出来时，他们已经把车钩上了，好吧，付掉放车费。

sentences.en: Pay it.
sentences.zh: 付钱。

sentences.en: Just pay it right then.
sentences.zh: 当场就付掉。

sentences.en: You're saving yourself time, aggravation, trouble, probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这能为你节省时间、减少烦恼、避免麻烦。

sentences.en: Just pay it.
sentences.zh: 付钱就行。

sentences.en: Try to negotiate it down.
sentences.zh: 试着讨价还价。

sentences.en: Say, you know what?
sentences.zh: 说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And this is what I tell people.
sentences.zh: 这就是我告诉人们的。

sentences.en: Let's say it's $400.
sentences.zh: 假设是400美元。

sentences.en: Say, oh, my God, would you take $250?
sentences.zh: 说，天哪，250美元行吗？

sentences.en: Barter, barter, barter.
sentences.zh: 讨价还价，讨价还价，讨价还价。

sentences.en: But get your car back.
sentences.zh: 但要把车拿回来。

sentences.en: Yeah, get your car back.
sentences.zh: 是啊，把车拿回来。

sentences.en: Don't leave it.
sentences.zh: 别把车留在那里。

sentences.en: Don't wait.
sentences.zh: 别等。

sentences.en: Don't wait.
sentences.zh: 别等。

sentences.en: We started with the question.
sentences.zh: 我们从这个问题开始。

sentences.en: How is it that you can just park your car at a 7-Eleven, 15 minutes later it's gone,
sentences.zh: 为什么你把车停在7-Eleven，15分钟后车就不见了，

sentences.en: and you have to negotiate a ransom with some guy in a dark parking lot, and that is an actual business?
sentences.zh: 然后你还得在昏暗的停车场里跟某个人讨价还价赎回车，而这竟然是一门正经生意？

sentences.en: And we have a pretty good answer.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有了一个相当不错的答案。

sentences.en: The reality is that towing regulation varies state by state.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，拖车法规因州而异。

sentences.en: But in many places, towing companies have contracts with private businesses to monitor and tow illegally parked cars in their lots.
sentences.zh: 但在许多地方，拖车公司与私人企业签订合同，负责监控并拖走其停车场内的违停车辆。

sentences.en: Some towers use spotters.
sentences.zh: 有些拖车公司会使用“盯梢者”。

sentences.en: Those are people who keep an eye on parking lots and call the tow company as soon as they see someone park there illegally.
sentences.zh: 这些人负责盯着停车场，一旦看到有人违停，就立即通知拖车公司。

sentences.en: Some tow companies don't post their fees and then bargain with people once they show up to try and reclaim their car.
sentences.zh: 有些拖车公司不公示收费标准，等车主来赎车时再进行讨价还价。

sentences.en: And in many states, there are few regulations governing how tow companies operate.
sentences.zh: 而且在许多州，几乎没有什么法规来约束拖车公司的运营。

sentences.en: With that, Kelly, consider your service request resolved.
sentences.zh: 好了，Kelly，你的服务请求已处理完毕。

sentences.en: Today on the show, you heard Kelly Prime, an editor with 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目中，你听到了99% Invisible的编辑Kelly Prime的讲述。

sentences.en: You also heard Tom Berry, a retired police officer who's now an investigator for the insurance industry.
sentences.zh: 你还听到了Tom Berry的讲述，他是一名退休警察，现在是保险行业的调查员。

sentences.en: And Shane Nation, a tow truck driver in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 以及底特律的拖车司机Shane Nation。

sentences.en: What infrastructure mystery keeps you up at night?
sentences.zh: 有什么基础设施方面的谜团让你彻夜难眠吗？

sentences.en: Is there something in your life that you use every day but you don't actually understand how it works?
sentences.zh: 你的生活中是否有什么东西是你每天都在用，却完全不明白它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Submit your service request by recording a voice memo with your question and emailing it to servicerequest at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 请录制一段语音备忘录提出你的问题，并发送邮件至 servicerequest@99pi.org 提交你的服务请求。

sentences.en: And remember, if your car gets towed, try to negotiate the price down.
sentences.zh: 记住，如果你的车被拖走了，试着去讨价还价。

sentences.en: Or better yet, don't get towed in the first place.
sentences.zh: 或者更好的是，一开始就别让车被拖走。

sentences.en: I'm Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 我是德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: Infrastructure is everywhere and we're here to help you decode it.
sentences.zh: 基础设施无处不在，我们在这里帮你解读它。
